source_text: Concaluit cor meum intra me; in meditatione mea exardescet ignis. Notum fac mihi Domine finem meum. Gloria Christo. Amen.
thought_title: The heart burns in meditation and asks to know its end
orientation: The psalmist, having just said he was silent and humbled, now speaks of his burning heart and asks the Lord to make known his end; Origen closes the section with a doxology to Christ.
pass_a_gloss: It grew hot [the] heart [of] me within me; in [the] meditation [of] me it will blaze out [a] fire. Known make to me O Lord [the] end [of] me. Glory [to] Christ. Amen.

choices.english: My heart grew hot within me
choices.why: Concaluit is perfect tense, so 'grew hot' preserves the completed action; 'within me' keeps the literal intra me rather than a smoother 'inside me'.
rejected: My heart was hot inside me
My heart became warm in me

choices.english: in my meditation a fire will blaze up
choices.why: Exardescet is future, so 'will blaze up' keeps the future force; 'in my meditation' follows the source word order and the glossary's 'meditation'.
rejected: a fire burns in my meditation
in my pondering a fire is kindled

choices.term: Notum fac mihi Domine finem meum
choices.english: Make known to me, Lord, my end
choices.why: Notum fac is a command, so 'Make known' keeps the imperative; 'my end' is literal for finem meum.
rejected: Lord, let me know my end

choices.why: Gloria with dative Christo is a standard doxological formula; 'Glory to Christ' is the literal rendering.

pass_b_english: My heart grew hot within me; in my meditation a fire will blaze up (Psalm 39:3). Make known to me, Lord, my end (Psalm 39:4). Glory to Christ. Amen.
